clue.text: Firm insisted, being in difficulties

parts.note: firm means hard, unyielding to the touch
to have insisted is to have pressed a point

explanation.surface: A company stood its ground on something while struggling to stay afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a business, but it is the adjective meaning solid; 'being' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone struggling under heavy pressure, short of time or money, is said to be in a tight spot of that kind.

clue.text: Cushion that fool found in debt?

indicators.note: found in means the word for fool is sitting inside the word for debt

parts.note: in hock means in debt
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A question whether a cushion belongs to an idiot who owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: In hock (pawned, owing) is informal for being in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm padded footstool for kneeling in church is a kind of cushion.

clue.text: Terms of reference for returning hunter perhaps

indicators.note: returning means the word for hunter is read backwards

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a protective cover, so an example of a timer

explanation.surface: Instructions given to a hunter coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter here is the pocket watch, not a person; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a timer.
explanation.definitionFit: The scope of an official's or committee's brief, the matters assigned to them, sets their scope.

clue.text: Quietly felt bitter when introduced

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly in music
resented means felt bitter about something

explanation.surface: Someone silently nursed a grudge on being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To be presented to someone is to be formally introduced, a synonym.

clue.text: Mephistopheles decapitated? That's bad

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: Mephistopheles is the devil of the Faust legend

explanation.surface: A remark that beheading the devil is a wicked thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked, morally wrong conduct is bad, a synonym.

clue.text: On board ship, a diner ordered fish

indicators.note: on board means placed inside the ship abbreviation, like passengers

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of diner are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger dining on a ship asks for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as a diner's request for food, but it is the anagram signal, making RDINE; 'On board' sets the whole inside the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Small oily fish often canned in oil are a common seafood.

clue.text: Hound master's strict doctrine

parts.note: a hound is a dog
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A dog owner's unbending set of rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a principle laid down as unquestionably true, a rigid belief.

clue.text: Reckoned a visitor ought to be listened to

indicators.note: to be listened to signals that the word for visitor is heard, spoken not written

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: Someone judged that a visitor deserved a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to estimate or suppose, so reckoned is a synonym.

clue.text: The way boxing permit can be a risky game?

indicators.note: boxing means the way encloses permit, as in a box

parts.note: a route is the way to go
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A suggestion that allowing boxing makes a dangerous sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gamble on a spinning wheel is a chancy pastime.

clue.text: Restaurant employee in battle line? That's right!

parts.note: the Somme was a great First World War battle
a line spun to someone is a story, an untruth

explanation.surface: A waiter appears to have been at a front-line battle, and someone confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme (a river in northern France) gives its name to the 1916 battle; a 'line' in the sense of a smooth patter is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter who advises diners on bottles is a specialist member of restaurant staff.

clue.text: Fumble for cord on key

indicators.note: in this clue the cord is placed after the key, so on signals following it

parts.note: G is a musical key
a rope is a thick cord

explanation.surface: Someone fumbling for a string attached to their keyring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key, but it is the musical key of G.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel about blindly with the hands is to fumble.

clue.text: Beginning to expose group

parts.note: to out someone is to expose their secret
a set is a group of things belonging together

explanation.surface: An instruction that the first step is to unmask a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The very start of something is its opening moment.

clue.text: The sort of events for which claimers are trained?

indicators.note: trained suggests the word claimers has been drilled and reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wry question about what people who make claims are coached to expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' reworks the letters of CLAIMERS; the question mark covers the loose definition by kind of event.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonders that seem to defy natural law are a sort of event people claim to witness.

clue.text: Catherine welcomes artist's skill in combat

indicators.note: welcomes means Catherine takes the artist in, holding him inside

parts.note: Kate is a short form of the name Catherine
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A woman named Catherine admires a painter's prowess as a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' signals a container: the host takes the guest inside. Royal Academicians are crossword's standard artists.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese martial art of strikes and kicks is a fighting skill.

clue.text: Inspire confidence if users are confused

indicators.note: confused says the letters of users are have been muddled

explanation.surface: Advice to calm customers who are puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to remove their doubts and fears, giving them trust.

clue.text: Left — in fact forced to leave!

indicators.note: in places the word for left inside the word for fact

parts.note: a deed is a fact, as in the phrase in deed
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone simply went away, but really they were expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the definition, a past tense, but it is the nautical sense, the left side of a ship. 'in deed' is an old phrase meaning in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone expelled from a country by official order has been made to go.

clue.text: Run off some bowling with a medicine ball

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so overs are some bowling
a pill is a small ball of medicine

explanation.surface: A cricketer's training session with a heavy exercise ball.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is six deliveries in cricket; a 'medicine ball' is a gym weight, but here it is a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Overflow, excess that runs off the edge, is spilling over.

clue.text: Ring for directions to theatre seats

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north
the circle is an upper tier of theatre seats

explanation.surface: Asking the way to where you'll be seated at a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround it completely, a synonym.

clue.text: The reputation of a parliamentary candidate?

explanation.surface: A question about how highly an election hopeful is regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a candidate stands for Parliament rather than runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Status or good name is how someone is rated; a candidate putting themselves up for election is doing so in the British idiom.

clue.text: Trains fish

explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach them; groups of fish swimming together are shoals.

clue.text: It was found in the lecture centre of late

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words lecture centre, waiting to be picked out

explanation.surface: A remark that something was discovered at a lecture hall not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened lately is fresh, not long past.

clue.text: Politician (English) in trial creating a storm

indicators.note: in places the politician and English inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An English politician on trial causes an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent gale, a synonym for storm.

clue.text: Say their doctor gets a panic attack?

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means tamper with, so the letters of say their are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient's doctor seems to be having a sudden fit of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning tamper with, rearranging SAY THEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild uncontrollable emotion, an outburst of frenzied fear, matches a sudden bout of panic.

clue.text: Provides comfort stops when leader goes

indicators.note: when the leader goes, the first letter of the word for stops is removed

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: A comfort break on a journey once the guide has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comfort stops' reads as toilet breaks, but 'stops' is CEASES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or worry is to soothe, relieving distress.

clue.text: Retreat when harm is possible

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: possible suggests harm is only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A warning to withdraw whenever there is a risk of injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' signals that the letters can be rearranged, giving HRAM; 'when' is a common crossword stand-in for 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious community where people withdraw from the world is a spiritual refuge.

clue.text: At home wrapped in a blanket feeling sorry

indicators.note: wrapped in means at home goes inside the blanket

parts.note: a rug is a blanket
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone at home under a blanket feeling sorry for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so regretting is feeling sorry.

clue.text: Friends who have equipment start helping

parts.note: kit is equipment

indicators.note: start means the first letter of helping

explanation.surface: Pals who own the gear begin pitching in.
explanation.walkthrough: KITH survives mainly in the phrase 'kith and kin', friends and family.
explanation.definitionFit: Kith are one's acquaintances and neighbours, close companions.

clue.text: Turn back and rescue half from the monsters

indicators.note: back means the word for turn is read in the other direction

parts.note: your go is your turn in a game

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters of rescue are used

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to retreat and save half the people from fiends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn back' looks like one instruction, but 'Turn' is GO and 'back' reverses it to OG.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-eating giants of fairy tales are fearsome brutes.

clue.text: Is it Circe who turned to find fault?

indicators.note: turned means the letters of is it and circe are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether the enchantress Circe turned critical.
explanation.walkthrough: Circe, the sorceress who turned men into pigs, makes 'turned' look like her magic; it rearranges IS IT CIRCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise is to point out faults or complain about someone.

clue.text: Understand, but boil with anger before match, for example

indicators.note: before places the word for anger ahead of the word for match

parts.note: to seethe is to boil with anger
a match is one kind of light, used to start a fire

explanation.surface: A sports fan fuming before the game starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sports fixture, but it is a match that gives a light.
explanation.definitionFit: To finally grasp the truth is to have a sudden realisation, an idiom for comprehension.
